Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Migration follow-up: deployment mode recommendations (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Samir / Anika,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on Lumina's mixed stack. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap of needs:
- Current stack: OpenAI-hosted API for general prod traffic; an on-prem GPU cluster for PHI workflows.
- Goals: reduce per-token cost on high-volume routes, meet latency SLOs for end-user-facing endpoints, and ensure PHI never leaves Lumina-controlled environments.
- Constraints: procurement cycle (~6–8 weeks), security/compliance checklist (SOC2 + network diagrams), and a hard requirement to isolate PHI workloads to private infrastructure.

Recommended staged approach:
1) Pilot on Redwood Hosted API (2–4 weeks) — validate prompts + latency, quick to start (low friction).
2) Dedicated capacity for high-volume production routes — predictable throughput & lower unit cost; can be reserved via monthly commit.
3) Private VPC / on-prem for PHI — customer-managed networking + KMS; we can support an air-gapped on-prem package if needed.

What we'll need from Lumina to scope this properly:
- Monthly token estimate (prompt + completion), expected peak rps, and typical seq length / max tokens per call.
- Network contact for VPC peering / direct connect (if going Private).
- Any export-control or additional compliance artifacts early.

I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP_draft_v1.pdf) and a short SOC2 summary for your security team. I've also pulled a preliminary Dedicated pricing sheet (dedicated-pricing.xlsx) to give a sense of the economics between Hosted vs Dedicated.

If this approach sounds reasonable, propose two next steps: 1) technical deep-dive with Marcus (SE) to go through connectivity and model options; 2) procurement kickoff to start SOW/pricing review. Are you free for a 60-min SE call next Tue/Wed (Oct 13/14)?

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Migration follow-up: deployment mode recommendations (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Great — thanks for the details and the numbers, Samir. That volume and peak behavior maps well to the Dedicated capacity profile (predictable throughput + better cost per token at scale).

Staged plan w/ rough timing:
- Pilot (Hosted API): 2–4 weeks to validate prompts, latency, and QA — minimal integration work.
- Dedicated reservation: provisioning and baseline config typically 3–4 weeks after signed commit (provisioning includes autoscaling and model variant selection).
- Private VPC/on-prem for PHI: network + security review + peering typically 4–6 weeks in parallel; on-prem air-gapped packaging can be scheduled after a scoping call.

Notes on migration from OpenAI/self-hosted cluster:
- For non-PHI traffic, we can do a phased DNS/routing cutover from OpenAI to Redwood Hosted, then move to Dedicated once traffic patterns are stable.
- For PHI: keep traffic on-prem or route to a private VPC. We support a routing policy that classifies requests and sends PHI-tagged requests to your private endpoint.
- We'll provide a migration playbook (prompt tests, traffic split guide, canary rollout steps) as part of the MAP.

Next items I will action: 1) loop Marcus (SE) + Neha (CS) to schedule the deep-dive and prepare a migration playbook sample; 2) share the security questionnaire link and full SOC2 report for your InfoSec; 3) prep a redline-friendly SOW/pricing doc.

Can Marcus join the Oct 13 call at 10:00am PT? If so I'll send the invite.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marcus / Neha — forwarding the thread with Lumina (Samir / Anika). Please see notes and action items below ahead of the Oct 13 SE deep-dive (10:00am PT).

Key context:

- Requirements: PHI must remain in Lumina-controlled environment. They want cost reduction for high-volume routes and predictable latency.

SE ask list (please prepare):
1) VPC connectivity options: peering, Direct Connect/Cloud Interconnect patterns, expected latency ranges, and firewall/network requirements.
2) Routing policy demo: show how we can tag/classify and route PHI traffic to a Private VPC while sending non-PHI traffic to Dedicated/Hosted.
3) Model variants & quantization: recommended quantization/profile for their seq lengths to optimize cost and latency tradeoffs.
4) Migration playbook outline: DNS cutover steps, canary percentages, rollback plan, and monitoring hooks (tracing/latency/quality guards).
5) Any blockers for SOC2/network artifact collection. We'll hand them the SOC2_Summary.pdf and a link to the full report.
